conformal.note: Adaptive coverage is realised online: the level is updated from each outcome after that row has been predicted, which is what the method does in deployment. It is not a held-out score.
conformal.statement: Calibrated on validation for 90% coverage, split conformal delivers 83.2% on the test period and decays year by year to 73.1% in 2026; adaptive conformal holds 90.0% overall and within half a point of target in every year, paying for it with sets that grow from 0.91 labels to 1.08.

evaluation.accuracy_note: Accuracy is excluded: at this base rate, always answering "no anomaly" scores 88.7% and predicts nothing.

explainability.note: SHAP values are in log-odds. The base value is -3.0292, which is 0.0461 as a probability.

cities_not_held_out.auckland: no labelled rows past the feature warm-up
cities_not_held_out.buenos_aires: no labelled rows past the feature warm-up
cities_not_held_out.johannesburg: no labelled rows past the feature warm-up
cities_not_held_out.sydney: no rows in the test split; its record ends 2021-09-01

leave_one_city_out.trained_on: every other city's train and validation splits

verdict.statement: Held out of training entirely, each of the 11 scored cities is still ranked better by the model than by its own persistence baseline (11 of 11, median PR-AUC 1.65x persistence and 107% of the same city's in-sample score), so the model transfers to a city it has never seen.

leave_one_city_out.yardstick: that city's own persistence baseline, not its base rate

calibration.recommendation_note: Isotonic on validation halves the calibration error and is worth shipping. The prior shift is not: its EM estimate of the target prior is badly biased here, and no choice among the candidate quantifiers can be made on validation. See quantifier_diagnostics.

calibrated.what: isotonic fitted on validation, applied to test

calibrated_prior_shifted.what: and re-weighted to the prior EM estimates on the target period

prior_shifted_oracle.what: NOT SHIPPABLE: re-weighted to the observed test prior, to show what the correction is worth when the estimate is right

hazard.target: P(first anomaly on day t+k | none through t+k-1)

recency.measured_from: the last day of the training split
recency.normalised: to mean one, so min_child_weight means the same thing at every half-life
recency.rule: better PR-AUC and better Brier, or the unweighted fit stands
recency.weighting: exponential in the age of the row

verdict.statement: Adding the four teleconnection indices moves validation PR-AUC by -0.0101 and test by +0.0404; they help 6 of 11 cities on validation and 9 of 11 on test. They do not ship: the decision is made on validation, which does not support them.

threshold_sensitivity.statement: Re-run at |Z| thresholds 2, 2.5, 3, the recommended model beats every baseline on PR-AUC and Brier at all three, and on F1 at some but not all of them.
